source.title: Neural computations of threat in the aftermath of combat trauma

confidence_rationale: Combat veterans on threat reversal learning: PTSD symptoms scale with prediction-error weighting for negative outcomes, which shapes associability; striatal (not amygdala) tracking of associability partially mediates the effect, and amygdala tracks value. Supports aversive associability as a computational variable with clinical consequence; mixed on locus relative to Li 2011.
failure_signatures: Exaggerated weighting of aversive prediction errors produced higher associability and more PTSD symptoms, so an associability mechanism without a bound on PE weighting predicts a trauma-like over-learning phenotype.
Here striatum tracked associability and amygdala tracked value -- the reverse of Li et al. 2011 -- so the anatomical locus of aversive associability is not settled.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In combat veterans, symptomatic individuals showed greater physiological adjustment to unexpected negative outcomes (larger PE weights), which shaped cue associability and value; striatal tracking of associability partly mediated the PE-weight/PTSD correlation, and reduced amygdala value tracking and smaller amygdala volume independently predicted severity.
mapping.ree_translation: Gives MECH-598 a psychiatric failure mode: if the aversive PE gain on associability is too high, candidate causes stay highly learnable and threat predictions over-update -- a PTSD-like phenotype. That is a useful pre-registered sign for a V3 arm (over-generalisation is already one of the claim's falsifiers).
mapping.mapping_caveat: Clinical correlational sample; the locus finding conflicts with Li 2011, so neither should be cited for anatomy. Associability is fitted, not manipulated.
mapping.source_context: Human fMRI and structural MRI, combat veterans, Pavlovian threat reversal with shock, hybrid PH/RW modelling

confidence_components.notes: Good venue, moderate clinical N, correlational. Mapping moderate: supports associability as a variable and adds a phenotype, not a mechanism.
